quizQuestions.prompt: What does Ephesians 2:8-9 say salvation is, so that no one can boast?
quizQuestions.explanation: "By grace are ye saved through faith... it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast."

options.text: A gift of grace through faith, not of works
A reward for perfect obedience to the law
Available only to the Jewish people

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Ephesians 6 tell believers to put on for spiritual battle?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil."

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Ephesians 6:12, what does Paul say believers really wrestle against, not flesh and blood?
quizQuestions.explanation: "We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world."

options.text: Spiritual powers and rulers of darkness

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Ephesians 4:32 instruct believers to be toward one another, forgiving as God forgave them?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you."

options.text: Kind and tenderhearted, forgiving one another
Cautious and suspicious of each other
Silent about wrongs done to them

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Ephesians 2:10 call believers, created in Christ Jesus for good works?
quizQuestions.explanation: "We are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works."

quizQuestions.prompt: What comparison does Ephesians 5:25 make about how husbands should love their wives?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church."

options.text: As a master loves a servant
As a king loves his kingdom
As a soldier loves his weapon

quizQuestions.prompt: What do believers have through Christ's blood, according to Ephesians 1:7?
quizQuestions.explanation: "In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins."

quizQuestions.prompt: What roles does Ephesians 4:11 list as gifts Christ gave the church for building up believers?
quizQuestions.explanation: Apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers -- given for the perfecting of the saints.

options.text: Apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and teachers

quizQuestions.prompt: Where was Paul when he wrote the letter to the Ephesians, describing himself as "the prisoner of the Lord"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ephesians is one of Paul's "Prison Epistles," written while he was imprisoned.

options.text: In his own home in Tarsus

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Ephesians 3:20 say God is able to do, "exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think"?
quizQuestions.explanation: It describes God's power to work far beyond what believers can imagine.

options.text: Work exceeding abundantly above all we ask or think
Grant exactly what is requested, nothing more

quizQuestions.prompt: What list of "ones" does Ephesians 4:4-6 give to describe the unity of believers?
quizQuestions.explanation: "One body, and one Spirit... one Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all."

options.text: One body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God
One temple, one priest, one king
One law, one land, one language
One city, one throne, one crown

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Ephesians 2:14 say Christ broke down between Jew and Gentile?
quizQuestions.explanation: "He is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition."

options.text: The veil of the Temple only

quizQuestions.prompt: What well-known verse from Philippians 4:13 speaks of strength through Christ?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me."

options.text: "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Philippians 4:6-7 promise will guard our hearts if we pray instead of worrying?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds."

quizQuestions.prompt: What repeated command does Philippians 4:4 give, twice in the same verse?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Philippians 1:21 declare about life and death for Paul?
quizQuestions.explanation: "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain."

options.text: "To live is Christ, and to die is gain"
"To live is gain, and to die is loss"
"Both life and death should be feared"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Philippians 2 say Christ did, taking "the form of a servant" and humbling Himself?
quizQuestions.explanation: Christ made Himself of no reputation, took the form of a servant, and humbled Himself even to death on a cross.

options.text: He humbled Himself, even to death on a cross
He demanded worship as a king
He remained in heaven the whole time

quizQuestions.prompt: What is unusual about where Paul was when he wrote this consistently joyful letter?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul wrote Philippians from prison, yet the letter is filled with joy and encouragement.

options.text: He wrote it from a royal palace
He wrote it while sailing to Rome
He wrote it during a great feast

quizQuestions.prompt: What has Paul learned to be, according to Philippians 4:11-12, "in whatsoever state" he finds himself?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Philippians 3:13-14 say Paul does regarding his past, pressing toward a prize?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Forgetting those things which are behind... I press toward the mark for the prize."

options.text: Forgets what's behind and presses forward
Dwells constantly on his past mistakes
Refuses to move forward at all
Returns to his old way of life

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise does Philippians 4:19 give about God supplying believers' needs?
quizQuestions.explanation: "My God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus."

options.text: God will supply all their need
God will supply only what is deserved
Needs must be earned through labor alone
No promise about needs is given

quizQuestions.prompt: Which church, founded by Paul with Lydia among its first converts, did he write this warm, affectionate letter to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul wrote to the church at Philippi.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Colossians 1:15-17 say about Christ's role in creation?
quizQuestions.explanation: "By him were all things created... and by him all things consist."

options.text: By Him all things were created and hold together
He was created after the angels
He had no part in creation
He created only the earth, not the heavens

quizQuestions.prompt: What attitude does Colossians 3:23 say work should be done with, "as to the Lord"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Colossians 2:8 warn believers not to be taken captive by?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men."

quizQuestions.prompt: What qualities does Colossians 3:12-13 tell believers to "put on," including forgiving one another?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mercy, kindness, humbleness, meekness, longsuffering, and forgiveness.

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Colossians 1:18 give Christ in relation to the church?
quizQuestions.explanation: "He is the head of the body, the church."

options.text: The head of the body, the church

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Colossians 3:2 instruct believers to set their affection on?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth."

quizQuestions.prompt: Which church, one Paul had not personally founded or visited, is the letter to the Colossians addressed to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul wrote to the church at Colosse (Colossae).

quizQuestions.prompt: Which "beloved physician" does Paul mention in his closing greetings in Colossians 4:14?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul mentions Luke, "the beloved physician," confirming Luke's profession and closeness to Paul.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Colossians 3:16 say should dwell in believers richly, through psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly."

quizQuestions.prompt: Like Ephesians and Philippians, where was Paul when he wrote Colossians?
quizQuestions.explanation: Colossians is also one of Paul's Prison Epistles, written during his imprisonment.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 describe happening to "the dead in Christ" at His return?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive... shall be caught up together with them in the clouds."

options.text: They shall rise first, then the living are caught up together
They remain in the grave forever

quizQuestions.prompt: What three commands does 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 give about rejoicing, praying, and giving thanks?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks."

options.text: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in everything
Fast constantly, remain silent, avoid others
Work without rest, never pray, complain often
Sleep little, speak little, give little

quizQuestions.prompt: What comparison does 1 Thessalonians 5:2 use to describe how the day of the Lord will come?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night."

options.text: As a thief in the night
After a written warning to all

quizQuestions.prompt: Why does Paul say he writes about believers who have died, in 1 Thessalonians 4:13?
quizQuestions.explanation: So they would not sorrow "even as others which have no hope."

options.text: So they would not sorrow without hope
So they would stop grieving entirely
So they would forget the departed
So they would fear death more

quizQuestions.prompt: Which major Macedonian city, where Paul had briefly ministered before being forced to leave, is this letter addressed to?
quizQuestions.explanation: The letter is addressed to the church at Thessalonica.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Paul remind the Thessalonians about his own conduct among them, so he wouldn't be a financial burden?
quizQuestions.explanation: He reminds them of his "labour and travail: for labouring night and day" while ministering to them.

options.text: He labored night and day so as not to burden them
He demanded payment for his teaching
He lived off the church's wealth
He refused to work at all

quizQuestions.prompt: What three parts of a person does 1 Thessalonians 5:23 pray would be preserved blameless?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless."

quizQuestions.prompt: What is 1 Thessalonians considered to be, chronologically, among Paul's New Testament letters?
quizQuestions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians is considered one of Paul's earliest letters, possibly the earliest.

quizQuestions.prompt: What principle does 2 Thessalonians 3:10 give about work and eating?
quizQuestions.explanation: "If any would not work, neither should he eat."

options.text: If a man will not work, he should not eat
All food should be shared regardless of work
Only the wealthy should eat well

quizQuestions.prompt: What misunderstanding about Christ's return was Paul correcting in his second letter to the Thessalonians?
quizQuestions.explanation: Some believed the day of the Lord had already come, causing confusion and even some to stop working.

options.text: That the day of the Lord had already come
That the church had failed entirely

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Paul pray for the Thessalonians in 2 Thessalonians 1:11, regarding their calling?
quizQuestions.explanation: He prays God would count them "worthy of this calling."

options.text: That God would count them worthy of their calling
That they would return to Jerusalem
That their persecution would end immediately

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Thessalonians 3:16 call the Lord, asking Him to give peace "always by all means"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Thessalonians 3:3 say about the Lord's faithfulness toward believers?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil."

options.text: He will establish them and keep them from evil
He is faithful only to the wealthy
He has no promise of protection

quizQuestions.prompt: How does 2 Thessalonians compare in tone and topic to Paul's first letter to the same church?
quizQuestions.explanation: It continues themes about Christ's return, but focuses on correcting confusion and addressing idleness.

options.text: It corrects confusion about Christ's return and idleness
It abandons the topic of Christ's return entirely
It introduces an entirely new gospel
It is addressed to a different city

quizQuestions.prompt: What encouragement does 1 Timothy 4:12 give to Timothy about his age?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers."

options.text: "Wait until you are old to lead"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Timothy 6:10 say is "the root of all evil"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The love of money is the root of all evil."

quizQuestions.prompt: What church office does 1 Timothy 3:1-7 list qualifications for, involving character more than skill?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul lists qualifications for a bishop (overseer/elder).

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Timothy 2:5 say there is one of, between God and men?
quizQuestions.explanation: "There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus."

quizQuestions.prompt: What relationship did Paul describe having with Timothy, calling him his own in the faith?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul referred to Timothy as his true/beloved son in the faith.

options.text: A spiritual son in the faith

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Timothy 4:8 say is more profitable than bodily exercise?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Timothy 6:12 urge Timothy to fight, laying hold on eternal life?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life."

quizQuestions.prompt: What humble title does Paul give himself in 1 Timothy 1:15, regarding his past as a persecutor?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul calls himself "chief" of sinners, showing deep humility about his past.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Timothy 3:15 call the church, using two images of stability?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The pillar and ground of the truth."

options.text: The pillar and ground of the truth

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous final words does Paul give in 2 Timothy 4:7, near the end of his life?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith."

options.text: "I have fought a good fight... kept the faith"
"I can do all things through Christ"
"To live is Christ, to die is gain"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Timothy 3:16 say about all Scripture?
quizQuestions.explanation: "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness."

options.text: It is given by inspiration of God and is profitable
It is only useful for scholars

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Timothy 1:7 say God has NOT given believers, contrasting it with power, love, and a sound mind?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Timothy 2:15 urge Timothy to "study" to be, needing not to be ashamed?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed."

options.text: Approved unto God, a workman unashamed

quizQuestions.prompt: Who were Timothy's mother and grandmother, praised for a genuine faith that Timothy inherited?
quizQuestions.explanation: Eunice (mother) and Lois (grandmother) are praised for their unfeigned faith.

quizQuestions.prompt: Where was Paul when he wrote 2 Timothy, considered one of his very last letters?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul wrote from prison in Rome, near the end of his life, awaiting execution.

quizQuestions.prompt: How does Paul describe himself in 2 Timothy 4:6, near his death, saying he is ready to be "offered"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul describes his time of departure as "at hand," comparing himself to a drink offering being poured out.

options.text: Ready to be offered, his departure at hand

quizQuestions.prompt: Who does Paul ask to be brought to him near the end of 2 Timothy, saying he is "profitable to me for the ministry"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul asks for Mark to be brought to him.

quizQuestions.prompt: On which island did Paul leave Titus to set things in order and appoint elders?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul left Titus on Crete.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Titus 2:11-12 say has appeared to all men, teaching them to live soberly and godly?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men."

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Titus 3:5, how were believers saved, not by works of righteousness?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us."

options.text: By great wealth given to the poor

quizQuestions.prompt: What kind of relationship did Paul have with Titus, similar to his relationship with Timothy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Titus was Paul's trusted spiritual son and co-worker in ministry.

options.text: A spiritual son and trusted co-worker

quizQuestions.prompt: What surprising thing does Paul do in Titus 1:12-13, quoting a description of Cretans as liars and "slow bellies"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul quotes a Cretan prophet/poet, showing his willingness to use secular sources to make a point.

options.text: He quotes a secular Cretan source
He praises all Cretans without question
He refuses to discuss Crete at all
He orders Titus to leave Crete immediately

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Titus 3:1 remind believers to be toward governing authorities?
quizQuestions.explanation: "To be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates."

quizQuestions.prompt: Philemon, Paul's shortest letter, is a personal appeal on behalf of which runaway slave?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul writes on behalf of Onesimus, who had fled from Philemon.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Paul ask Philemon to do regarding Onesimus, who had since become a believer?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul asked Philemon to receive Onesimus back not as a slave, but as a beloved brother.

options.text: Receive him as a brother, not a slave

quizQuestions.prompt: How does Paul describe himself at the opening of the letter to Philemon?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul describes himself as "a prisoner of Jesus Christ."

quizQuestions.prompt: What generous offer does Paul make regarding any debt Onesimus owes Philemon?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul offers to personally repay anything Onesimus owed.

options.text: To personally repay the debt himself
To have the debt forgotten by force
To let Onesimus stay enslaved until it's paid
To ask the Roman court to cancel it

quizQuestions.prompt: What relationship did Philemon have with Onesimus before Onesimus fled?
quizQuestions.explanation: Philemon was Onesimus's master/owner.
